notes: v1.14.536 — LEGACY-RETIRE STAGE 3.1: THE LEGACY HEADER IDENTITY BLOCK. The PHANTOM wordmark (.app-logo / #appLogoTap) and the .app-loc site line are removed, with their CSS, the two guarded writers that filled .app-loc, and the dev escape hatch bound to the wordmark. Both elements were display:none under body.rd — the redesign's identity is .wmimg + #rd-sub — so this is invisible in the redesign and VISIBLE under ?legacy=1, where the header-left now renders empty. ⛔ Two findings drove the shape of this ship. First, deleting the element without its handler would have left `if (!logo) { setTimeout(bind, 500); return; }` retrying every 500ms for the life of every session, in both houses — so the handler went first. Second, v1.14.210's LOGO-HOME single-tap-to-Command-Center was gated redesign-only and bound to an element the redesign hides: dead on arrival for 326 versions, and it goes out with the element. The 5-tap boot replay went too — it was legacy-reachable only, for the same reason. ⛔ SCOPE CORRECTED MID-STAGE: #hdr-overflow-wrap was dropped from this ship's plan. The Stage 3 recon listed it from a body.rd display:none grep, but it contains the legacy overflow MENU — export, restore, identity, hardware reference, and legacy_returnToNewUI, the only way back out of the ?legacy=1 rip-cord. Deleting it would strand anyone who entered legacy.
